deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§35–36 of E477). Euler studies the 'singular' series q^m = Σ_{k≥1} k^{-m}(1 + 2^{-n} + … + k^{-n}) = Σ_k H_k^{(n)}/k^m, which is ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n) in modern double-zeta notation. He writes p^s for ζ(s). In each row the first term p^{λ−ν} is shorthand for the product p^{λ−ν}·p^{ν}, and the column labelled p^{2j+1} stands for the product ζ(2j+1)ζ(λ−2j−1). On the previous page he worked out the weight λ = m+n = 11 table and noticed that its coefficients are binomial coefficients of exponent λ−2, read once downward and once upward and then added.

Notation on this page. He introduces n(ν) = C(n,ν) and notes three facts: n(ν) = 0 for ν > n, n(n) = 1, and n(ν) = n(n−ν).

The general formulas. For odd weight λ he lists the rows q^{λ−1}, …, q^{λ−5} and then states the general rule, with m = λ−ν and n = ν:
- Odd ν: S(λ−ν, ν) = ζ(λ−ν)ζ(ν) + ½(1 + C(λ,ν)) ζ(λ) ± Σ_{j≥0} [C(2j,ν−1) + C(2j,λ−ν−1)] ζ(2j+1) ζ(λ−2j−1).
- Even ν: S(λ−ν, ν) = ½(1 − C(λ,ν)) ζ(λ) ∓ Σ_j [same binomial pairs] ζ(2j+1) ζ(λ−2j−1).
- The next page adds that the sum stops at the column p^{λ−2}.

The divergent ζ(1) column. The j=0 column contains the formally divergent ζ(1)ζ(λ−1). Its job is to cancel the leading product ζ(λ−1)ζ(1) when ν = 1, or to vanish because the binomials are zero. Euler thus handles ζ(1) as a formal symbol that drops out.

What it is. This is Euler's classical theorem: for odd weight, every linear Euler sum, equivalently every double zeta value, reduces to ζ(λ) plus products of zeta values. He expresses this in closed binomial form.

Checks.
- λ = 11 table, row q^9 (ν = 2): column p^9 gives 8(1) + 8(8) = 8 + 1 ✓; column p^3 gives 2(1) + 2(8) = 2 ✓.
- Same table, row q^8 (ν = 3): column p^9 gives 8(2) + 8(7) = 28 + 8 ✓.
- λ = 5, ν = 2: true value Σ H_k^{(2)}/k^3 = 3ζ(2)ζ(3) − (9/2)ζ(5), and ½(1 − 10) = −9/2 ✓.
- λ = 5, ν = 1: true value Σ H_k/k^4 = 3ζ(5) − ζ(2)ζ(3), and ½(1 + 5) = 3 ✓.
- λ = 3: Σ H_k/k^2 = 2ζ(3) ✓, but only if the ζ(1) column carries a minus sign.
errors: Sign inconsistency in the printed general formulas. For odd ν the brace (product) terms must carry a MINUS sign and for even ν a PLUS sign. This is what the λ=11 table on p.182 shows (row q^10: −1,−1,…; row q^9: +2,+4,…), and it is what correctness requires: Σ H_k/k^2 = 2ζ(3) needs the ζ(1)ζ(2) term to cancel, and Σ H_k^{(2)}/k^3 = +3ζ(2)ζ(3) − (9/2)ζ(5). On this page (and in Case I on p.184) the odd-ν rows are printed with '+' and the even-ν rows with '−', i.e. the signs are swapped. The coefficient ½(1 ± λ(ν)) of p^λ is correct. Read literally, the general statement is wrong in sign. Whether this is a misprint or Euler's slip I cannot tell; the Opera omnia editors may have noted it (unsure).

Notational ambiguity rather than an error: 'p^{λ−ν}' in the first term and 'p^{2j+1}' in the columns denote products with the complementary zeta value (p^{λ−ν}·p^{ν}, p^{2j+1}·p^{λ−2j−1}). This is not stated on this page.
The j=0 column formally contains ζ(1). It is only meaningful because it either cancels the leading ζ(λ−1)ζ(1) term (ν=1) or has zero binomial coefficient. The formula is formal at that point.

ideas.what: Closed binomial formula reducing odd-weight linear Euler sums Σ H_k^{(n)}/k^m to ζ(m+n) and products ζ(a)ζ(b)
ideas.modern_name: Euler's reduction theorem for double zeta values / linear Euler sums of odd weight
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1775/76); rigorous modern proofs by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) and Flajolet–Salvy (1998)
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Commentarii Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20 (1776); Opera omnia I.15

ideas.what: Notation n(ν) for binomial coefficients, with the remarks n(ν)=0 for ν>n and n(ν)=n(n−ν)
ideas.modern_name: binomial coefficient C(n,ν) and its symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Euler used this bracket-style notation elsewhere

ideas.what: Formal use of the divergent ζ(1) as a symbol whose terms cancel
ideas.modern_name: formal regularization of ζ(1) in double zeta relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: modern regularization theory (Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier 2006) for systematic treatment

missed.claim: The general formula as printed has the signs of the product terms swapped relative to Euler's own λ=11 table and to the correct values. Odd ν needs −, even ν needs +. Modern citations that transcribe the formula directly from this page would inherit the error.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only a minor erratum in a famous formula, relevant for historically faithful citation. It is likely already noted by editors; unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: This page states Euler's well-known odd-weight Euler-sum reduction, which is fully credited to him in the modern literature. The only notable item is an apparent sign inversion in the printed general formula.
transcription_corrections: The 'p^{s}' superscripts in the scan are the old-type numeral 5 (p^5), as the transcription correctly renders.
In the first line the scan reads 'n(2)' (rendered with a glyph resembling 'n(7)'); the transcription's n(2) is correct.
The transcription matches the scan in signs ('+0(0)' in odd rows, '−0(1)' in even rows). The mathematical sign issue lies in the original print, not in the transcription.
